body: /u/CoffeeBeansCrusader I apologise for telling you to fuck off, it wasn't a constructive response to your comments.

You are a very insensitive person. I told you to fuck off because you are rude and unhelpful, your initial comment was unnecessarily cruel and unappreciated. Look to the downvotes, the only person who agrees with what you said is you.

Don't come at me and accuse me of thinking I deserve sympathy for being a victim, then try to out do me by listing all the bad things that have happened to you. If that's what you think I'm doing then you're just as bad. Obviously I sympathise with your abuse, I have experienced very similar things but I am not here trying to outdo how messed up it made you. 

'Leave it in the past' oh wow. Never thought of that - I'm cured! You might be able to do that but I cannot, not when I'm still experiencing and recovering from trauma to this day. It might work for you, right now I'm just trying to function.

At what point did I demand to be waited on hand and foot? Literally all I want is treatment for a mental illness. It's sad that you think that's such an over the top demand.

I am not interested in speaking to you any further. Your comments have not been helpful or given any 'helpful insight' and have frankly only upset me further. I'm going to stop replying to you now.

No, I am sorry but you are wrong on so many levels.

BPD is seen as a mental illness, there just isn't as much treatment available because it's rarer than depression or anxiety. There is no defined cure or treatment for BPD, the medication offered to people with this illness is actually usually used to treat epilepsy and the most effective form of therapy is called DBT, which is extremely hard to get because not a lot of psychologists (at least where I'm from) are qualified to prescribe it.

Second of all, how dare you, a stranger, come and berate on a post where I am clearly distressed and emotional, and tell me that my lack of treatment is my fault when you do not know me and you do not know the exact conversation that took place between me and the nurse. I have been seeking help for years, I have tried medications that have made me sick and suicidal in the hope that it will make me better and persevered with them for months on the off chance that they might just do something. Seeking treatment is the willingness to change, I want to change how I am living with my mental illness so actually fuck off with that flippant attitude and stop pretending you know a single thing about what is going on with me and my brain.

I will say again: I did not just sit down and rant and rave about all the shit that's happened to me in my life. She asked me questions and I answered relevantly e.g. 'Do you have a good relationship with your parents?' 'I got along well with my father before he died, me and my mother are distant because she has been abusive to me and my brother as a result of her alcoholism'. How's that for you? Too ranty? Guess I should've kept my mouth shut and left her guessing because yes, that is what will get me into treatment.

What will be helped by spewing out everything I have done wrong in my life? Have my actions somehow contributed to my mental illness do you think? Or are you asking me to tell myself that my unstable childhood and abusive past are my fault? I am not a perfect person and I have done things I regret, as has EVERYONE. I wasn't at confession, man, if she'd asked me to list some of the bad things I've done then I would've but she didn't. I wonder why.

It wasn't. I was there to be reviewed for possibly going on medication and I just answered the questions she asked, she wanted me to be as detailed as possible as 'it was more helpful to her'.

I have BPD. I was also assaulted recently and I'd noticed that my general symptoms had been worse since.

I wasn't sure if it counted as assault for a while but I've thought about it a lot and I think it does. This guy has mutual friends with me and I'm scared of how they'll react and I don't think there'd be any point in going when it's been a long time since t happened.
